_comment: IAW status/bitfield decoders. 'enum' = value maps to one label; 'bits' = value is a bitmask, list every set flag. 'base' = radix of the keys. Attach to a param in params.json via {"map":"<name>","map_type":"enum|bits"} once the status-carrying rli is identified; the raw value is still logged.

fuel_mode._note: 0x58 is the fuelling mode, one number out of twelve, not a bitfield (firmware read 2026-10-08). The bitfield reading it replaces happened to fit the only values the rides produced: 5 and 7 are the two idle modes, which is why '0x01 = closed throttle' tracked the throttle, and 6/7 are 2/5 with fuel cut-off armed, which a timer enables some 30 s after the start -- the '0x02 after-start phase over' bit measured on 2026-09-08. Decoded as bits, 2, 3, 4 and 8-11 would have been mislabelled. 3/4 and 8/9 are entered on a deceleration or acceleration event, 10/11 are the overrun cut-off and the fuel return after it.

clutch._note: polarity verified on the bike 2026-09-04: the ECU answers 0 while the lever is pulled (the engine was started that way) and 1 with it released -- the reference table had it the other way round

runstate._note: 0x57 across 2026-09-09. 4 stands while the engine runs (732 of the 733 samples above 500 rpm) and the kill button takes it to 8, which the rider watched happen. 16 stood for two samples at the instant of one stop and arrived 18 s after another. The firmware read of 2026-10-08 gives the whole set: 1 power-up, 2 ignition on with no crank signal, 4 turning, 8 the crank signal lost with the ignition still on, 0x40 the ignition switched off while the engine still turns, 0x10 ignition off and waiting for the engine to stop, 0x20 the shutdown that saves the learned data. So 16 is 'ignition off', no longer a guess.

kill_run._note: 0x7A and 0x79 were strictly inverse across all 261 samples where both were read on 2026-09-09, with no (0,0) or (1,1) pair anywhere, while the rider worked the kill switch. The firmware read of 2026-10-08 shows 0x7A is not the switch itself but the ECU's run enable, which spark and injection wait on: it is worked out from the inputs, and in the code it drops with the side stand down and a gear engaged, with the 0x77 input at 0, and on speed and rpm conditions. Its link to the kill switch is the measured one above; the two stay inverse only while nothing else blocks the engine.

kill_stop._note: 0x79 is the kill switch itself, 1 at STOP. 0x7A (kill_run) is the run enable the ECU works out from its inputs: on the bike the two have been strictly inverse, but only because nothing else was blocking the engine -- with the side stand down and a gear engaged 0x7A drops while 0x79 stays at RUN.

lambda_ctl._note: 0x4B on 2026-09-08 (1130 same-state pairs), split by the sign of the 0x47 integrator step: 7 rises 266 times against 32 with the sensor at a median 175 mV (lean), 5 falls 200 against 35 at a median 727 mV (rich), and both carry 0x49 = 2 -- the two branches of the closed loop, 231 and 228 transitions between them. 4 is open loop with the integrator held (57 of 120 steps flat, 0x49 = 0), 3 is the same but transitional and rare, 1 is the controller frozen with the engine stopped (124 of 125 steps flat) and 2 only shows on a cold sensor (39-63 mV, integrator at 0). 0 and 6 were never seen, so they carry no label.

lambda_loop._note: 0x49 on the 2026-09-04 warm-up: a flat 0 for the first 43 s from cold, then 0<->2 at the rate the sensor itself switches -- 2 is the closed-loop correction being applied

idle_mode._note: 0x62 across the 2026-09-10 ride (693 samples): 0 only with the engine stopped, 4 only with the engine running and the throttle at its 1.6-2.0 deg stop (1168-2234 rpm), 2 everywhere else (1223-5053 rpm, throttle out to 25 deg). The three do not overlap, which is what the guessed label already said.

throttle_zone._note: 0x5C is the throttle zone (firmware read 2026-10-08): 1 closed, 4 part throttle, 2 wide open. The edges are not fixed angles: they hang off the learned closed and open stops of the sensor, with hysteresis -- in to 'closed' 0.2 deg above the closed stop, out at 0.6 deg -- which is why no fixed throttle threshold at any lag agreed better than 92 % on 2026-09-10. (0x5C == 4) == (0x6A > 0) in 680 of 693 samples that day because 0x6A is computed only outside the closed zone; 2 needs the throttle near its open stop, which that ride never reached.

fans._note: 0x70, firmware read 2026-10-08. Bit 0 and bit 1 are the two fan outputs, bit 2 is set when both are on, bits 3 and 4 are the two fan requests. The request turns on at 98 C coolant with the engine running (and on some sensor faults); the rides so far topped out at 96-97 C, which is why the channel read a flat 0. On a Granpasso the second output is used for the lambda heater, so bits 0, 2 and 4 are expected to stay clear.
